paper_a.title: A sharp threshold for a random version of Sperner's Theorem

paper_b.title: A container theorem for general digraphs with forbidden subdigraphs

metadata.description: Both papers deploy the container method but in very different theorems. Balogh-Krueger build bespoke weak/strong containers tailored to the middle-two-layers bipartite graph $M$ to prove a sharp probabilistic threshold for the random Sperner problem (largest antichain of $\mathcal{P}(n)_p$ lives in a middle layer w.h.p. for $p>3/4$). Liu instead applies the Saxton-Thomason hypergraph container theorem off-the-shelf, after a degree estimate, to obtain a container theorem for $H$-free digraphs satisfying a sparsity Condition A. The papers share the high-level container template (cover all 'forbidden-substructure-free' configurations by few near-extremal containers) but differ entirely in target theorem, the auxiliary hypergraph constructed, and whether containers are built ad hoc or imported.

matches.explanation: These are the central container-existence statements of each paper. Balogh-Krueger's weak (LP429.2) and strong (LP429.3) container lemmas produce, for the middle-two-layers bipartite graph $M$, a small family $\mathcal{W}_t$ of pairs $(S,F)$ that simultaneously covers every 2-linked $A\in\mathcal{A}_t$ (with concentration of $|S\cap X|,|F\cap X|$ and $|S|\le|F|+\varepsilon t$). Liu's main container theorem (TP441.3) and its KOTZ predecessor (TP441.1) likewise produce a small collection $\mathcal{C}$ of digraphs covering every $H$-free digraph with $e_a(G)\le\mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\varepsilon N^2$ and $\le\varepsilon N^h$ copies of $H$. The role is the same (cover all forbidden-substructure configurations by a near-extremal family of size $\exp(\varepsilon t)$ resp. $\exp(cN^{2-1/m(H)}\log N)$); the targets differ entirely (bipartite-poset expansion vs.\ digraph-Turan-type counting).

Both are the technical heart of their respective papers. TP429.3 is the two-layer expansion theorem on $V(M)_p$ deduced from the strong container lemma via union bound. TP441.3 is the digraph container theorem deduced from Saxton-Thomason via the degree estimate. Both are 'main technical results' obtained by combining a container-construction step with a counting/union-bound step, but the assertions are mathematically unrelated (random expansion of bipartite shadows vs.\ deterministic enumeration of $H$-free digraphs).

Balogh-Krueger's definition of weak/strong containers (DP429.13) — pairs $(S',F')$ with $A\subseteq S'$, $F'\subseteq N(A)$, slack $O(t)$ resp.\ $\le|F|+o(t)$ — is the bipartite-graph analogue of the 'container collection' $\mathcal{C}$ that appears as output in Liu's TP441.1/TP441.3 (digraphs $G$ with $I\subseteq G$ and $e_a(G)$ near extremal). Both encode 'cover the forbidden-substructure configuration by a near-extremal envelope', but DP429.13 is a bespoke definition for the bipartite middle-layers setting rather than a hypergraph independent-set-style container.

Both are technical 'control quantities' driving the container construction. Balogh-Krueger's $(\varepsilon,t,p)$-concentrated collection (DP429.12) measures uniform deviation $||Y\cap X|-p|Y||\leq\varepsilon t$ across a family of subsets — the property the container collection must satisfy for the union bound to close. Liu (via Saxton-Thomason) uses the codegree function $\delta(\mathcal{H},\tau)$ (DP441.4), the central quantity that must be small for the Saxton-Thomason container theorem to apply. The roles are analogous (a key uniform-control parameter guarding container existence) but the underlying objects (random concentration vs.\ deterministic codegree) differ substantially.

Both are the key 'expansion / degree' estimates that make the container construction go through. LP429.1 lower-bounds the boundary expansion $t=|N(A)|-|A|\ge\frac{a}{k}\log\frac{\binom{2k-1}{k}}{a}$ for any $A\subseteq L_k$ — controlling the cost of encoding $A$ in the container scheme. LP441.1 bounds the codegree function $\delta(\mathcal{D}(N,H),\tau)$ of the auxiliary hypergraph encoding $H$-copies, exactly the input Saxton-Thomason needs. Both serve as the quantitative 'feeder' lemma into the container-existence step, but they bound different quantities (poset expansion vs.\ hypergraph codegree).

These are the proof-level container constructions. PP429.9/PP429.10 build the weak / strong container family for the middle-two-layers graph $M$ from scratch (introduce intermediary sets $R,T,L,F',Q,R',Q',S'$, then $H,F'',S'',U,S,F$, with cost/concentration bookkeeping). PP441.2 instead proves the main digraph container theorem by feeding the codegree estimate into Saxton-Thomason and translating containers from the auxiliary hypergraph $\mathcal{D}(N,H)$ back to digraphs. Both are 'proof of the container lemma' at the L1 level, but the construction is hand-rolled in paper A vs.\ delegated to Saxton-Thomason in paper B.

Each is the proof of the paper's 'feeder' bound that is later plugged into the container step: PP429.1 proves the expansion bound LP429.1 by Kruskal-Katona plus a one-variable monotonicity check; PP441.1 proves the codegree bound LP441.1 by a five-step argument (crude bound, structural refinement using $m(H)$, summation, derivation of $\delta_j$, geometric series). Both are short technical proofs supporting the main container construction; the underlying mathematics is unrelated.

The main result of Balogh-Krueger (TP429.1: sharp threshold $p>3/4$ for the random Sperner problem) is a probabilistic structural theorem with no analogue in Liu's deterministic enumeration / container framework.

The hitting-time theorem TP429.2 (for $p>1/2$, every largest antichain of $\mathcal{P}(n)_p$ consists of one near-middle layer plus nearly isolated sets) is paper-A-specific structural content with no counterpart in Liu's container theorem for digraphs.

LP429.4 is the general-layer (all $k\ne\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$) expansion lemma derived from TP429.3 via Kruskal-Katona — a paper-A-specific reduction to the middle-layers case. No analogue in Liu.

LP429.7 (small-$|A|$ regime expansion in $X$, complementary to the strong container lemma in the large-$t$ regime) is bespoke to Balogh-Krueger's strategy of splitting the proof of TP429.3 by $|A|$ size. Liu's proof has no such regime split.
LP429.6 is a deterministic poset-shadow estimate $|N(A)|\geq ka-\binom{a}{2}$ for small antichains, used to feed LP429.7. No counterpart in Liu's digraph container setting.
PrP429.5 (expansion outside the middle: $|\partial A|\geq(1+1/k)|A|$) is a deterministic Boolean-lattice expansion estimate with no Liu analogue.

The 'cost facts' (PrP429.1), auto-concentration for tiny sets (PrP429.2), union/difference concentration (PrP429.3), and the Chernoff-based concentration criterion (PrP429.4) form Balogh-Krueger's bespoke 'concentration calculus' for derived collections of the middle-layers graph. They have no counterpart in Liu's paper, which delegates all such bookkeeping to Saxton-Thomason.

Balogh-Krueger's three-consecutive-layers conjecture for $p=\omega(1/n)$ is a paper-A-specific open problem; Liu's open question (OpenP441.1) concerns a different topic (characterising digraphs admitting a container theorem).

Equation EP429.1 defines $\mathcal{A}_t$, the family of 2-linked subsets of $L_k$ with prescribed expansion deficit $t$. This is the bipartite-poset object containers are built around; Liu's analogous 'object indexed by deficit' is the digraph $G\in\mathcal{C}$ itself, but no separate equation-level definition in paper B mirrors EP429.1.

Antichain / width, Boolean lattice / layers, random subset $A_p$ / w.h.p., coarse vs.\ sharp threshold — the basic poset-and-probability vocabulary of paper A. None of these have analogues in Liu's deterministic digraph framework.
Isolated and nearly isolated sets are the 'exceptional configurations' that the random Sperner argument must rule out. They have no counterpart in Liu's digraph framework.

Closed sets and 2-linked sets in a bipartite graph are the structural restrictions used by Balogh-Krueger to control which $A\subseteq L_k$ need containers. Liu has no analogous 'closed / 2-linked' filter; the digraph container construction applies to all $H$-free digraphs.

The middle-two-layers bipartite graph $M$ on $\binom{[2k-1]}{k}\cup\binom{[2k-1]}{k-1}$ is the central host structure of paper A. The host structure of paper B is the auxiliary hypergraph $\mathcal{D}(N,H)$ (DP441.5), which is a fundamentally different (deterministic, hypergraph-of-copies-of-$H$) object and is captured separately.
$\ell$-chain in a poset is a paper-A definition used to phrase the antichain condition; no Liu analogue.

Cost / conditional cost of a derived collection is paper A's bespoke entropy-like accounting tool for tracking how much information is needed to describe each $A\in\mathcal{A}_t$ given prior choices. Liu has no analogous explicit 'cost' framework — that role is hidden inside the Saxton-Thomason black box.
Lower / upper shadow definitions $\partial_*A$, $\partial^*A$ are poset-specific. No Liu analogue.
Closure $[A]$ and 2-linked component definitions are bespoke to the bipartite-poset setting of paper A.

Degree to a set $d(v,Y):=|N(v)\cap Y|$ is a basic graph notion paper A uses when constructing the strong container by trimming high-degree-defect vertices. No paper-B node singles out such a degree-to-set notion.

Bespoke claims used inside the proof of the weak container lemma (LP429.2): existence of a good random subset $R$, of $R'\subseteq T\setminus G$, and the size bounds on $|S'\setminus A|,|G\setminus F'|,|A\setminus Q|$. These are internal to paper A's hand-rolled construction and have no Liu analogue (Saxton-Thomason hides such intermediate combinatorial choices).
Internal claims of the strong container lemma proof (PP429.10): bounds on $|H|$ and on $|U|$ with $U\subseteq N(S'')$. Bespoke to paper A's construction.

Proofs of the union/difference concentration (PrP429.3), Chernoff-based concentration (PrP429.4), and outside-middle expansion (PrP429.5) propositions. They are technical paper-A propositions in the bespoke concentration calculus and have no Liu counterpart.
Proof of LP429.4 (general-layer expansion) reduces to the middle-two-layers theorem TP429.3 plus Proposition PrP429.5 and a union bound over $k$ — paper-A-specific reduction with no Liu analogue.
Proofs of the main theorems TP429.1 and TP429.2: push-down / hitting-time arguments specific to the random Sperner problem. No Liu analogue.
Proof of LP429.7 (small-$|A|$ regime expansion in $X$) is paper-A-specific.

Proof of TP429.3 combines LP429.7 (small $a$) with LP429.3 (large $t$ via strong containers) and a tailored union bound. The 'apply container lemma + union bound' pattern is loosely parallel to Liu's PP441.2, but the small-$a$ vs.\ large-$t$ decomposition, the explicit cost bookkeeping via $A^*$, and the $|S|\le|F|+\varepsilon t$ slack handling are entirely paper-A-specific. The high-level analogue of PP441.2 has been recorded above against PP429.9/PP429.10; emitting another match here would be redundant.

Weighted size $e_a(G)$ and weighted Turan number $\mathrm{ex}_a(n,H)$ are the digraph-Turan vocabulary that drives Liu's main theorem. They have no analogue in Balogh-Krueger's poset / threshold framework, where the relevant quantity is the size of an antichain in $\mathcal{P}(n)_p$.
Definition of a 2-cycle (double edge) in a digraph — basic vocabulary specific to the digraph extremal setting; no Balogh-Krueger analogue.

Auxiliary hypergraph $\mathcal{D}(N,H)$ encoding labelled copies of $H$ as $r$-edges is the central construction that lets Liu reduce to Saxton-Thomason. Balogh-Krueger work directly with the bipartite middle-layers graph $M$ (DP429.9) and have no analogous auxiliary $r$-uniform construction.

Condition A (sparsity bound $e(H')/v(H')\le a/2$ for all subgraphs $H'\subseteq H$ with $e(H')>1$) is the structural hypothesis that lets Liu's argument go through. Balogh-Krueger's analogous structural hypothesis is 'closed and 2-linked' for $A\subseteq L_k$, but they are conceptually different (sparsity of $H$ vs.\ connectedness of $A$).

Density parameter $m(H)=\max_{H'\subseteq H,e(H')>1}\frac{e(H')-1}{v(H')-2}$ controls the exponent $N^{2-1/m(H)}$ in Liu's container count. There is no Balogh-Krueger parameter that plays this role; their container-count exponent $\varepsilon t$ is parameterised differently.

Liu's enumerative corollary $f^*(n,H)=2^{\mathrm{ex}_2(n,H)+o(n^2)}$ (counting labelled $H$-free digraphs) is a deterministic counting statement; Balogh-Krueger pursue a probabilistic structural threshold instead and have no such corollary.
Liu's open problem (characterise digraphs admitting a container theorem) is paper-B-specific.
